findings.title: A text field's change now ends a press in every keepLive region, and the planner then rebuilds the Map under the pointer: the click after editing a node's text can be lost
findings.where: scripts/live.mjs:306-307 (onChange releases on any change in the region); scripts/investigation.mjs:1883-1900 (write on change, then forced refresh); rule 1 for a hand, live.mjs:120-131 (E44 C2b, S10-58)
findings.what_happens: Rule 1 for a hand holds a region from pointerdown to release so a rebuild cannot replace the control being clicked. A text field's change fires when it loses focus, which a pointerdown on another control causes (during mousedown, before pointerup). The new onChange takes that change as the press being over and releases it. The planner's new change listener then writes the node's fields (a GM store write: a 0 ms timer and a client-setting write, gm-store.mjs:815-817, no server) and calls refresh(), a forced rebuild, within milliseconds, so the region (toolbar, node editors, Move buttons, Rests on boxes) is replaced before the pointerup. The comment at live.mjs:302-305 says 'no click follows it to lose its node', which is true for a select's pick, not for a text field left by a press on another control.
findings.evidence: live.mjs:306 `const onChange = event => { if (held && target()?.contains?.(event.target)) release(); };`; investigation.mjs:1888-1894 `saveFieldsIn(fields).then(() => { ... refresh();`; live.mjs:342 `stop.refresh = () => rebuild(true);`
findings.failure_scenario: A GM with every node open types a new name in a deduction, then clicks that deduction's Move down (or ticks a box in another node's Rests on, or presses Add deduction). The name is written and the Map redraws, but Move does not happen, or the box stays unticked; a second click works. On 1.2.119 the press held through the field's change (nothing was written until the GM left the Map), so the click landed.
findings.refutation_tried: Checked whether the press could still be held: onChange runs in the capture phase on the window root and calls release(), which clears `held` before the planner's bubble listener writes; with heldWanted false nothing is deferred. Checked whether the write is slow enough to land after pointerup: a schema node's write is a local GM store flush (0 ms timer), so refresh() comes within a few ms. Checked the tests: R1316 and R8012 dispatch no change from a text field under a press; the tier-2 node-field test dispatches change with no pointerdown; the Move tests call .click() with no press. Not run in a browser: that the click is then lost rests on the module's own E44 C2b reading (the delegated listener never heard the click on a replaced node), not on a run of this tree.

verifier.why: Measured in a real browser, no longer only suspected. With a text field of the region focused and changed, a real mouse press on another control of the region runs: pointerdown (live.mjs holds), mousedown, then the field's change (live.mjs onChange, capture, releases the press with nothing wanted), the planner's write, blur/focusout, focusin on the pressed button; the write lands about 15 ms later and refresh() is a forced rebuild with nothing holding it, so the region (toolbar, node editors, Move, Rests on) is replaced before the pointer is let go. Chromium then sends pointerup and mouseup to the new button but dispatches no click at all, to any target. On e515907d's live.mjs the same press holds through the change, the write's refresh is deferred ('a press inside it is not let go'), and the click lands; with e515907d's live.mjs and 1.2.120's planner write the click also lands, so the onChange release (live.mjs:306-307) is the cause and the planner's write-and-refresh (investigation.mjs:1883-1900) is what makes it bite. Narrower than 'can be lost' in one way only: it needs the write to finish before the pointer is let go. A deduction, counter or solution field writes through the GM store (setCaseNode -> store patch -> 0 ms timer -> client setting), about 15 ms here, so the click is lost at every press length tried (30, 60, 100, 150 ms). A Remnant's or Key slot's field writes the token on the server (setRemnantPublic), a race: modelled at 40 ms the click was lost, at 150 ms it landed. Also the store's own echo (clientSettingChanged, 120 ms debounce) would replace the region on its own for a press held longer than about 135 ms. Nothing is lost from the field (the typed name is written); what is lost is the second action, and a Rests on tick that silently did not happen can go unnoticed, which keeps it major. Not measured in Firefox or in Foundry's frame; Chromium is the engine of Foundry's desktop app.

findings.title: Move under By kind, room, state or fewer crossings re-sorts every other column
findings.where: scripts/investigation.mjs:2042-2045 (manual written for the moved column only, sort set to manual); scripts/case-layout.mjs:54-57 (a node with no manual place falls back to kind order); scripts/case-view.mjs:174 (every column now follows the sort)
findings.what_happens: moveCaseNode writes manual places for the moved column's nodes and sets the chapter's sort to manual. Every other column then orders by its nodes' manual places, which are absent (kind order) or stale from an earlier By hand. Since 1.2.120 every column follows the sort, so all of them jump, not only the first column as on 1.2.119.

findings.refutation_tried: Under the default By kind the other columns keep their order (kind is the manual fallback), so the jump needs another sort picked first. 1.2.119 had the same jump for column 0 only. The GM handbook (section 14) says only that the order set is the order drawn and the picker then reads By hand.

verifier.why: moveCaseNode (investigation.mjs:2022-2047) is unchanged from e515907d: it writes manual places for the moved column only and sets the sort to manual. The manual comparator (case-layout.mjs:54-57) puts a node with no manual place at Infinity and falls back to kindCompare, and since 1.2.120 every column under manual keeps the layout's order (case-view.mjs fixedOrder, packColumn fixed). So after a Move under By room, By state or Fewer crossings, every other column jumps to kind order or to stale manual places. On 1.2.119 only column 0 followed the sort (deduction columns centred on inputs whatever the sort), so only column 0 jumped; the finding's comparison is right. No guard or test pins the opposite. Under the default By kind no jump. Minor: the order is recoverable by picking the sort again, nothing is written to nodes.

findings.title: A dissolve let go by the bound, then a repaint that finds the picture unchanged, then the late end of that dissolve: no fog sprite is drawn

findings.what_happens: startDissolve hides the outgoing sprite and the incoming one and shows only the mix. When a repaint is asked more than fadeMs()+1750 ms after the start while the end has not run yet, queueBehindDissolve calls endDissolves (generation bumped, previous null) and returns false; repaintFog goes on, the signature equals lastPaintSignature (set when that dissolve began) and the layer is visible, so it returns 'unchanged' before swapInFog. When the old dissolve's end then runs it is stale: it drops the mix (mix.drpgTexture !== state.previous, which is now null) and returns without making its sprite renderable. The layer is left with the old and the new fog sprites both renderable=false: no fog at all until the next repaint whose signature changes. On e515907d the same sequence queued the repaint and the late end restored the new sprite.
findings.evidence: Driven on the module's own block with R8030's fake nodes (/tmp/r120-F/sim.mjs case 1): during the dissolve ['A:hidden','B:hidden','mix0:R']; let go, queued=false; after the late end ['A:hidden','B:hidden'], any renderable fog sprite: false.
